task: General sunflower frontier comparison; literature gate only
scope: Compare current general sunflower results with the claimed ordinary computer-assisted upper M(4,3)<=67 for simple arbitrary-support four-uniform families, forbidding three distinct sets with identical pairwise intersections, including an empty core.
outcome: No inspected general theorem directly supplies an arbitrary-support M(4,3)<=67 upper bound. This is a bounded source-search result, not an exhaustive priority certificate, proof-validity decision, review vote, or publication authorization.

primary_results.statements: Theorem 1: k>=3, N>=1, F subset of 2^[N], no k-sunflower => |F|<=3(2-1/(16k^3))^N. Theorem 2: V_k(D,n)<=((2k)^(2/(k-1)) D^(1-1/(k-1)))^n.
primary_results.parameter_comparison: N is support size, not uniform rank. At k=3 the first bound is 3(863/432)^N. A 68-member four-uniform family requires N>=8 since binomial(7,4)=35; already at N=8 this bound exceeds 760. The four-coordinate vector specialization is 1296 D^2 and is alphabet-dependent. Neither displayed theorem directly supplies <=67. Section 5 distinguishes the unsolved uniform problem and says the k=3 set bound does not improve Naslund–Sawin's exponential base.
primary_results.definition_match: Distinct members and arbitrary common intersection; empty core included.

primary_results.public_artifact_status: Author repository and matching PalomarArchive copy are publicly readable. This supersedes discovered aggregator statements that no public artifact was located.
primary_results.observed_scope: Solution.lean exposes exactly the vector bound, the support-size set bound, and one c_k<2 uniformly in admissible support sizes. Formalization metadata reports Lean4.35.0-rc2, no proof holes in Solution, standard axioms, and retained independent kernel logs. Challenge.lean intentionally contains statement holes and is not the proof.
primary_results.boundary: No compilation, replay, proof audit, or new verification was performed. README/metadata still describe preparation and no registration; existence of the archive is not alone evidence of registry endorsement. Neither code nor metadata claims M(4,3)<=67.

primary_results.version_seen: v1; returned primary HTML labels 17Jul2026 despite September identifier; retain raw metadata rather than normalize this discrepancy
primary_results.statement: An ell-bounded system with VC dimension<=d and no r-sunflower has size<=sum_{j=0}^ell (50dr)^j; in particular, an ell-uniform system of size>(50dr)^ell contains an r-sunflower.
primary_results.parameter_comparison: Every four-uniform family has VC dimension<=4. Taking ell=4,d=4,r=3 yields upper600^4=129600000000, far above67. The theorem does apply via bounded rank but does not supersede the claimed finite bound.

primary_results.statement: For an absolute C>0, every n-uniform family with VC dimension<=d and size>(Cr log(d+1))^n contains an r-sunflower.
primary_results.parameter_comparison: At rank4, petals3, VC dimension<=4, the expression is (3C log5)^4. The statement supplies no explicit C giving a67 bound; proof uses a spread constant>=1 and enlarges constants. This asymptotic refinement is relevant background, not a direct numerical replacement.

primary_results.version_seen: v2; revised2026-06-08; current title 'Erdos Rado Sunflower Theorem for Shifted Families'
primary_results.statement: For shifted families, f'(k,s)<=s^(2k) when k<=s-1, otherwise f'(k,s)<=2f'(k-1,s).
primary_results.parameter_comparison: The shifted-family hypothesis excludes direct application to arbitrary four-uniform families. The paper only controls sunflower-number growth under shifting by a factor2, not preservation of three-sunflower-freeness. Its displayed recurrence at k4,s3 gives324. Older indexed title/abstract claiming the unrestricted conjecture is stale.

primary_results.version_seen: v3; revised2026-06-22; comment says it fixes error ofv2
primary_results.statement: Claims existence of absolute c>0 such that |F|>(c k^4)^m forces a k-sunflower for sets of size at mostm.
primary_results.parameter_comparison: No explicit usable c supplies upper67 at m4,k3: displayed expression becomes(81c)^4. Treat as a source claim whose validity was not adjudicated. Current BHL discussion still describes unrestricted Erdos–Rado as open. No source-based basis here to convert this into priority against67.

primary_results.statement: For some C>=4, Sun(p,k)<=(Cp log k)^k for allp,k>=2.
primary_results.parameter_comparison: This is support-independent, but its bound at petals3, rank4 is far greater than67, even at the lower allowed C=4. Sun is a forcing threshold, so the extremal maximum convention differs by1.

primary_results.version_seen: 28September2026; no revision shown on inspected report page
primary_results.statement: Derandomized robust sunflower theorem for width-w monotone DNFs under pseudo-independent distributions. The sunflower conclusion is a high-probability residual-DNF property.
primary_results.parameter_comparison: Robust/distributional conclusion is not the exact three-petal relation. Inspected theorem has asymptotic parameters, no exact rank4 threshold67. No direct numerical replacement identified.

primary_results.version_seen: 22September2026; no revision shown on inspected report page
primary_results.statement: For k>=4 petals, a tensor faithfully realizing the set-sunflower relation on the full Boolean cube has maximal slice rank2^N; distinct-input variant has lower bound2^(N-k).
primary_results.parameter_comparison: A method obstruction, not a finite-family upper bound. Here4 means petals, not rank. It does not invalidate the BHL vector tester or address the target three-petal rank4 bound.

They do require accurate framing: no all-rank conjecture resolution, no first general AI-assisted sunflower result, and no claim that BHL formalization remains unavailable.
